subsystems.name: Engineered skin cells
subsystems.role: the living pixels — the patient's own skin cells carrying a light-emitting gene.

subsystems.name: Substrate supply
subsystems.role: bioluminescence needs a chemical fuel (luciferin) plus ATP, and a plant or animal body does not normally make it.
parts: luciferin or a precursor such as caffeic acid
recycling enzymes that regenerate the substrate

subsystems.name: Emission and tissue optics
subsystems.role: getting the light out through skin, which scatters and absorbs most visible light.
parts: high cell density in a thin layer

subsystems.name: Trigger circuit
subsystems.role: decides when a patch of cells lights up.
parts: activity-dependent promoter (for example a calcium- or c-fos-responsive element)
external override, such as a small drug

subsystems.name: Delivery and immune management
subsystems.role: puts the DNA in and keeps the body from rejecting the graft.
parts: lentiviral vector, transposon or CRISPR knock-in
safety screening for insertional cancer risk

buildSteps.title: Take a skin biopsy
buildSteps.detail: A few millimetres of the person's own skin is harvested and the keratinocytes and fibroblasts grown in culture — autologous cells avoid immune rejection.

buildSteps.title: Design the cassette
buildSteps.detail: A codon-optimised, red-shifted luciferase gene is combined with the enzymes of a substrate-recycling pathway and a trigger-responsive promoter.

buildSteps.title: Insert the DNA
buildSteps.detail: A lentiviral vector, transposon system or targeted CRISPR insertion carries the cassette into the cells; the goal is a small number of stable, mapped insertions.

buildSteps.title: Select and expand
buildSteps.detail: Successfully modified cells are isolated, checked for a single working copy, and multiplied into sheets tens of cells thick.

buildSteps.title: Graft onto the skin
buildSteps.detail: The sheets are placed on a prepared graft bed and take over days, forming a living layer under or within the epidermis.

buildSteps.title: Measure the light
buildSteps.detail: A calibrated sensor records how much light actually escapes the skin; emission, cell density and depth are adjusted until a patch is visible in a dark room.

buildSteps.title: Wire up the trigger
buildSteps.detail: The promoter is coupled to a local nerve signal — for example calcium entry or a released neurotransmitter — so the patch brightens when a chosen nerve fires.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the display
buildSteps.detail: Separate patches, each with a different trigger or promoter strength, are placed to give more than one independently controlled spot.

buildSteps.title: Monitor long term
buildSteps.detail: Regular sampling looks for uncontrolled growth and for fading of the signal as cells turn over.

prerequisites.why: genetically modified autologous skin has already been grafted onto patients to treat a severe blistering skin disease, proving engineered skin can survive on a person.
glowing plants and cultured cells have been made using a fungal pathway that recycles its substrate, but sustained brightness in a whole animal is much lower.
firefly and bacterial luciferases emit blue-green light that skin absorbs; longer-wavelength versions exist but are dimmer or need different fuels.

prerequisites.tech: Continuous luciferin supply in the body
prerequisites.why: lab imaging injects substrate and watches for minutes; a permanent display needs the body to make or continuously receive it.
promoters that switch on with neural activity are routine in brain research but have not been shown to work driving bioluminescence in skin.

pathway.milestone: bioluminescent cells and small animals used as laboratory imaging tools
pathway.unlocks: routine, sensitive detection of gene activity in living tissue.

pathway.milestone: engineered human skin grafts with a built-in light reporter, used clinically to show a graft is alive
pathway.unlocks: a medical reason to put light-emitting cells into people.

pathway.milestone: animal prototypes where a nerve signal makes a skin patch brighten
pathway.unlocks: proof that the trigger circuit works in living skin, not just in a dish.

pathway.milestone: multi-patch displays on consenting human volunteers
pathway.unlocks: a genuinely programmable body surface — limited by brightness through skin, substrate supply, safety review and the difficulty of controlling many independent spots.
